source.title: Polysemantic Experts, Monosemantic Paths: Routing as Control in MoEs
source.authors: Charles Ye; Bo Yuan; Lee Sharkey

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports results about polysemantic MoE experts, expert paths, and router-visible subspaces, but it does not test sparse-feature superposition, capacity competition, SAE features, or the dimensionality of superposed features as specified by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's routing probes, router-weight correlations, and channel analyses concern how MoE routing works, not whether sparse features overlap to fit limited dimensions. The path and cluster findings below are related results about expert-level and trajectory-level semantics, but do not measure a listed claim version.
record.test_reason: The paper studies MoE routing. It decomposes hidden states into router-visible and router-blind subspaces and shows that expert paths group tokens by function. It uses 'polysemantic' for whole experts, not neurons. It does not measure feature superposition, capacity competition, SAE features or feature dimensionality, and it does not cite the toy-model work. Expert-level polysemanticity attributed to low-bandwidth routing is a related but different construct from V2/V3, which concern neurons and features.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as paraphrased. The authors also report that the router-visible signal rotates across layers while content accumulates, and that surface features (language, token ID, position) sit mostly in the router-blind channel.
record.recipe_differences: Not a reproduction of the toy-model superposition method; the paper analyzes MoE routing subspaces and expert paths.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that channel-probe disparities are largest in middle layers and narrow at the earliest and final layers; its path analysis uses GPT-OSS-20B layers 8–16.

fits_no_version.finding: Paths of single experts across GPT-OSS-20B layers 8–16 group tokens into semantic-function clusters across languages and surface forms. The authors describe individual experts as polysemantic.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In MoE LLMs, multi-layer expert paths are more monosemantic units than individual experts.

fits_no_version.finding: Router-visible cross-layer clusters contain 4.3 unique token IDs, against 1.1 for router-blind and 1.4 for full hidden-state clusters, with ≥95% of clusters interpretable in each.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In MoE LLMs, the router-visible subspace organizes tokens by function, while the router-blind channel preserves lexical identity.

fits_no_version.finding: Across six MoEs, router weight magnitude correlates with hidden-dimension magnitude (ρ≈0.6). Probes using the top 2% of dimensions predict the top-1 expert with 30–80% accuracy, against 1–6% for random dimensions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MoE routers read mainly a small, high-magnitude subspace of the residual stream.

record.peer_reviewed: To appear at the ICLR 2026 Workshop on Representational Alignment (Re-Align)
record.problems: The cluster-diversity result uses 100 sampled clusters per subspace and 10 token samples per cluster; uncertainty for that result is not stated. The paper's findings concern MoE routing and paths rather than direct tests of feature superposition.
record.rows_left_out: None of the paper's other reported results was retained because they do not measure a listed claim version or a closely related expert/path semantic result.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity sweep or feature geometry.
All: no test of whether neurons share features because capacity is limited.
All: expert polysemanticity is described, but neuron polysemanticity and its causes relative to superposition are not tested.
All: no measure of features spread across neurons and no dictionary/SAE recovery.
All: no test of feature dimensionality.

record.verdict_notes: Rows r1 and r2 are correctly linked to no version; their values match the text (Section 4, Figure 4; 4.3 vs 1.1/1.4 unique IDs). The term 'polysemantic' applies to MoE experts, not neurons or features, so it does not bear on V2/V3. The paper's other results (Appendices D–F: router-magnitude correlation, probes, cross-layer cosine, channel MI probes) also bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions; overlap geometry; sparsity-dependent transitions.
Whether neurons share features because of limited capacity, and whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure or whether their polysemanticity is evidence against superposition.
Feature distribution across neurons in LLMs and sparse feature recovery with dictionaries or SAEs.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: GPT-OSS-20B
rows.operation_detail: Grouped tokens with identical top-1 expert paths across layers 8–16 and examined cluster semantics.

conditions.value: ∼10M multilingual tokens from C4 and HPLT; EN/ZH/ES

rows.measure: Semantic coherence of token groups sharing an expert path
rows.value: The authors report that paths form coherent semantic groups across languages and surface forms, including groups for exhibition-related terms, overseas terms, nutritional substances, and brand names.
rows.note: This is a result about expert-path semantics, not feature overlap or neuron-level polysemanticity.

rows.subject: GPT-OSS-20B
rows.operation_detail: Clustered tokens separately in router-visible, router-blind, and full hidden-state subspaces across layers, then measured lexical diversity.

conditions.value: 100 sampled cross-layer clusters per subspace; k=32

rows.baseline: Router-blind clusters: 1.1 unique token IDs per cluster; full hidden-state clusters: 1.4
rows.value: Router-visible clusters: 4.3 unique token IDs per cluster
rows.locator: Section 4, “The control subspace is the source”
rows.note: The paper describes router-visible clusters as grouping more diverse tokens by function; this is not a measurement of superposition geometry.

relation.reason: The paper discusses polysemantic experts and interpretable representations but supplies no test of feature overlap, capacity-driven neuron polysemanticity, dictionary features, or feature dimensionality.

tranche.reason: The study measures routing subspaces and expert-path semantics. It neither tests nor uses the listed superposition claims; expert polysemanticity concerns whole experts rather than neurons.
